literal: Later he was convicted for plotting rebellion with the monk Faxiu and was executed.
idiomatic: Later he was convicted of plotting rebellion with the monk Faxiu and was executed.

literal: His son Daoning was a palace attendant.
idiomatic: His son Daoning served as palace attendant.

literal: Sengyuan entered Wei territory; because of his brother he was exiled to Boguli Garrison; at the beginning of the Taihe era he was able to return.
idiomatic: Sengyuan came into Wei lands; on account of his brother he was exiled to Boguli Garrison and at the opening of the Taihe era was allowed to return.

literal: Emperor Gaozu heard he had learning and questioned him on Buddhist sutras; skilled in discourse, he ordered that though in lay dress he be granted a black headcloth and admitted to listen at the Yongle Jingwu Hall.
idiomatic: Gaozu heard of his scholarship, questioned him on Buddhist sutras, and found him skilled in debate; he ordered that though still in lay dress Sengyuan receive a black cap and attend lectures in the Yongle Jingwu Hall.

literal: Later Sengyuan was appointed Gentleman of the Protocol Section in the Secretariat.
idiomatic: Later he was made gentleman of the protocol section in the secretariat.

literal: After the move of the capital to Luoyang he was chief rectifier of Qingzhou.
idiomatic: After the capital moved to Luoyang he served as chief rectifier of Qingzhou.

literal: Soon he went out as staff counselor to the general who campaigns east, Grand General and Prince of Guangling Yu, with the additional title General of Illustrious Martiality; he attacked sea bandits at Huangguo [16] and inflicted a great defeat.
idiomatic: Soon he left court as staff counselor to the eastern campaign grand general, Prince of Guangling Yu, with the added title general of illustrious martiality; he attacked sea bandits at Huangguo [16] and routed them.

literal: Xiao Luan thereupon sent his clansman elder brother Huijing to leave a letter for Sengyuan, explaining the hardship of entering Wei and urging him to change course.
idiomatic: Xiao Luan then sent his elder clansman Huijing with a letter to Sengyuan, pleading the wrong of his coming into Wei and urging him to change his course.

literal: Sengyuan replied in writing:
idiomatic: Sengyuan wrote back:

literal: The sovereign's conduct as a man — nothing hidden escapes his light, nothing small escapes his care; in benevolence none so far he does not reach; in breadth no classic he does not exhaust; he exhausts the subtlety of the Three Storehouses and the utmost of the Nine Mounds.
idiomatic: Our lord's nature as a man leaves no dark place unlit and no small thing uncared for; in kindness there is no distance he cannot reach, in learning no canon he has not mastered — he has drained the subtlety of the Three Storehouses and the limits of the Nine Mounds.

literal: As for his literary compositions woven in complexity, brilliantly lustrous — they are like the Master's wall.
idiomatic: His woven prose blazes with color like the wall of the Master himself.

literal: Thereupon he opened the clarity of solitary awakening, traced the footprints of former kings, settled the desolate borderlands, presaged change in the imperial foundation, renewed the central lands, and dwelt facing the Yi domain.
idiomatic: He opened a solitary clarity of mind, traced the tracks of former kings, settled the wild marches, foretold change in the imperial foundation, renewed the central lands, and made his seat on the Yi banks.

literal: The three luminaries regained the illumination of renewed brilliance; the myriad things received the beginning of a second transformation.
idiomatic: The three lights shone again with renewed splendor; the myriad things received a second birth.

literal: He sorted clans and fixed descent, assessing grades of first and second class;
idiomatic: He sorted clans and fixed descent, grading households into first and second ranks;

literal: He arrayed offices and granted noble ranks, clarifying the thread of the nine currents.
idiomatic: he arrayed offices and granted noble ranks, clearing the thread of the nine currents.

literal: The ordering of ritual and custom blazed forth in revival; between the Yellow and Luo the Zhou Way was raised high again.
idiomatic: Ritual and custom blazed back to life; between the Yellow and Luo the Zhou Way rose again.

literal: Lane songs and district hymns, courts radiant and gates serene — such flourishing abundance cannot be fully set forth.
idiomatic: Lane songs and district hymns, radiant courts and tranquil gates — such flourishing cannot be told in full.

literal: Added to this, generation upon generation of doubled glory, a domain embracing the four sacred peaks, soldiers and horses strong and rich, men and spirits rejoicing in reverence — virtue, the Way, benevolence, and righteousness the people cannot name.
idiomatic: Add generation upon generation of doubled glory, a domain holding the four sacred peaks, strong hosts and rich stores, men and spirits rejoicing — virtue, the Way, benevolence, and righteousness beyond naming.

literal: Moreover when a great man appears, he has no fixed place of origin — how much more when one descends from the highest sage to Heaven's grandson?
idiomatic: When a great man appears he has no fixed birthplace — how much more one who descends from the highest sage to Heaven's grandson?

literal: [17] The sovereign's younger brothers share a matching bearing; from the Prince of Xianyang down, none without outstanding excellence; branches and leaves luxuriant, spread through the realm; that their renown is somewhat spent [18] is wholly premature.
idiomatic: [17] The sovereign's younger brothers share one bearing; from the Prince of Xianyang down, none without surpassing talent; branches and leaves spread through the realm — that their fame is already fading [18] is far too soon.

literal: Literati vie in counsel at the court; warriors display courage on the frontier — [19] if one reckons the true situation of affairs, this is the reality.
idiomatic: Scholars contend in counsel at court, soldiers show courage on the marches — [19] judge the true situation and this is fact.

literal: Consider the traces of that lord's usurpation and murder — known alike to men and spirits; suspicion of kin and mistrust of the noble long ago exposed far and near.
idiomatic: Weigh that lord's usurpation and murder — known to men and spirits alike; suspicion of kin and mistrust of the noble were long ago plain far and near.

literal: Elder brother, to cast your heart into rebellion — what name for a thousand years!
idiomatic: Elder brother, to set your heart on rebellion — what name will stand for a thousand years?

literal: When things have no scope for use and vessels are unfit for the time, one who lives without stirring the age and dies without a fair reputation — the former masters held this base, gentlemen held it shameful.
idiomatic: When things have no place to be used and vessels are unfit for the age, to live without stirring the world and die without a fair name — the ancients called that base, gentlemen called it shame.

literal: Here events are straitened and skills exhausted; self-exhortation brings no gain — hence the fit course.
idiomatic: Here affairs are tight and arts spent; urging oneself on brings no gain — hence the proper course.

literal: With elder brother's talent, from old surpassing your homeland — who among men like me does not look up to you? Whenever I recall former thoughts, I dare not forget.
idiomatic: With your talent, elder brother, you have long outshone our homeland — who like me does not look up to you? I never dare forget our old bond.

literal: Though the road spans two thousand li, in thought we meet face to face; reverently I follow the norm and draw on it for a lifetime.
idiomatic: Though two thousand li lie between us, in thought we meet as face to face; reverently I follow your example for my whole life.

literal: Now fame could be raised yet you cannot glorify kin; affairs could be changed yet you cannot leave disgrace — hence what the age has not understood.
idiomatic: Now fame could be raised yet you cannot honor your kin; affairs could be changed yet you cannot shake off disgrace — that is what the age cannot understand.

literal: And the gentleman at home does no more than show filial piety to his kin; in court does no more than show loyalty to his lord.
idiomatic: A gentleman at home is filial to his kin; in court he is loyal to his lord — no more.

literal: The sovereign's treatment of elder brother — in grace it cannot be repaid, in righteousness it cannot be betrayed.
idiomatic: The sovereign's treatment of you, elder brother — grace that cannot be repaid, righteousness that cannot be betrayed.

literal: The person may be killed — hence this is not the repayment;
idiomatic: One's person may be given up — that is not repayment;

literal: Merit does not reach so far — hence this is not the return.
idiomatic: merit does not stretch so far — that is not return.

literal: Now you could effect loyalty yet again do not — this is unfilial.
idiomatic: Now you could act loyally and again you will not — that is unfilial.

literal: Judged by fact, elder brother's not changing — can this count as loyalty?
idiomatic: Judged by fact, elder brother, can your refusal to change count as loyalty?

literal: As for training in arms and contending for supremacy, the unmatched have long been so;
idiomatic: As for drilling in arms and contending for mastery, you have long been unmatched;

literal: Discussing security and danger, those not alike have been proved;
idiomatic: weigh safety against peril and the unlike cases have been proved;

literal: Mass sentiment turns away in desertion; to remain alone is error.
idiomatic: the crowd's heart has turned away — to stand alone is error.

literal: [20] I beg deep scrutiny of this.
idiomatic: [20] I beg you to weigh this deeply.

literal: Wang Yan utterly cut off external ties; his capacity was not heroic and bright; clinging to splendor and guarding hope, he was at once sent to slaughter.
idiomatic: Wang Yan cut off every outside tie; his talent was not bold and bright; clinging to glory and nursing hope, he was at once put to the sword.

literal: Compared with elder brother, you are whole a hundredfold.
idiomatic: Compared with you, elder brother, he was not one part in a hundred.

literal: Moreover the Huai lands and the coastal marches originally produced northern champions — could elder brother escape the charge at Shouchun?
idiomatic: Moreover the Huai frontier and the coastal garrisons bred northern champions — could you, elder brother, escape the Shouchun command?

literal: On this ground, suspicion and mistrust are already settled.
idiomatic: On that ground suspicion is already fixed.

literal: Moreover the ancestral house is not many generations old; north and south have no other lodging — to whom but elder brother can the weight of the prior structure be entrusted? The glory of receiving a fief — this humble heart has longed for it.
idiomatic: Moreover the house is still young; north and south have nowhere else to lodge — to whom but you, elder brother, can the weight of the founding be entrusted? The glory of receiving a fief — my humble heart has long looked for it.

literal: Now clinging to resolve without waking, both filial piety and loyalty forgotten — Wang Yan's crime, how can he protect himself? To act when the moment appears — is it not here?
idiomatic: Now you cling to your resolve without waking, forgetting both filial piety and loyalty — Wang Yan's guilt, how could he save himself? To act when the moment shows itself — is it not now?

literal: The state from Chang'an in the west to Jimo in the east — forging armor and weapons — all to utmost solidity and keenness; day and night without cease for these several years.
idiomatic: The state from Chang'an in the west to Jimo in the east has forged armor and weapons to utmost solidity and keen edge, day and night without cease these several years.

literal: In the middle month of autumn this year the cloud net will surely rise; goods that miss the season, though costly, are not used — if you do not plan early, what of wronging a linked city?
idiomatic: This mid-autumn the cloud-net will surely be cast; goods that miss the season, though precious, are not used — if you do not plan early, how will you answer for a city worth a thousand?

literal: [21] Mei Cheng said: wanting to go out yet not going out, no space between for a hair — how refined that saying!
idiomatic: [21] Mei Cheng said: wanting to go out yet not going out — no room for a hair between — how fine that saying!

literal: Your younger brother struck at Beijing, personally suffered penal summons; that the Great Making reached me was fortune obtained.
idiomatic: Your younger brother was struck down at the northern capital and personally bore penal summons; that the great grace reached me was luck won.

literal: Recently I have been repeatedly promoted by clear selection beyond counting — [22] the heart of dog and horse truly has its place.
idiomatic: Lately I have been raised again and again by clear selection, more than once — [22] the heart of dog and horse truly has its master.

literal: Though now we stand on opposite sides, the old feeling is unchanged — how much more today?
idiomatic: Though we now stand on opposite sides, the old feeling is unchanged — how much more so today?

literal: Like elder brother's teaching, like younger brother's counsel — to change the tuning and reset the strings is easier than turning the palm; if feeling should once go awry, that will be fate.
idiomatic: As elder brother teaches, as younger brother urges — to change the tuning is easier than turning the palm; if feeling should once go wrong, that will be fate.

literal: He went out and was dismissed as Dragon-Charging General and Inspector of Southern Qingzhou.
idiomatic: He left court as dragon-charging general and inspector of Southern Qingzhou.

literal: After long time, convicted of campaigning out without warrant; investigated and confined; later he was pardoned.
idiomatic: After long service he was convicted of campaigning out without warrant, investigated and imprisoned; later he was released.

literal: Sengyuan's first wife, Lady Fang, bore two sons, Bolin and Boji.
idiomatic: Sengyuan's first wife, the Fang clan, bore two sons, Bolin and Boji.

literal: Later he slighted the Fang clan and took the Du clan of Pingyuan in marriage.
idiomatic: Later he slighted the Fang and married the Du of Pingyuan.

literal: When Sengyuan was exiled he went with Du and bore four sons: Bofeng, Zulong, Zuchi, and Zuqiu.
idiomatic: When Sengyuan was exiled he went with Du and she bore four sons — Bofeng, Zulong, Zuchi, and Zuqiu.

literal: After his return he abandoned Lady Fang and settled in Qingzhou with the Du clan and the four sons.
idiomatic: After he returned he cast off the Fang and made his home in Qingzhou with Du and the four sons.

literal: Boji lived with his mother Lady Fang in Jizhou; though he went back and forth to his father, his heart remained with his mother — filial and kindly duty was suddenly blocked within one gate.
idiomatic: Boji lived with his mother the Fang in Jizhou; though he visited his father, his heart stayed with his mother — filial kindness was cut off within one household.

literal: Sengyuan died at over seventy.
idiomatic: Sengyuan died aged over seventy.

literal: Bolin though he hurried to the funeral did not dare enter the house and wept at a Buddhist temple.
idiomatic: Bolin hurried to the funeral but dared not enter the house and wept at a Buddhist temple.

literal: Bolin, from court attendant, was gradually promoted to infantry commandant and governor of Leling, with the additional title general of the central guard.
idiomatic: Bolin rose from court attendant to infantry commandant and governor of Leling, with the added title general of the central guard.

literal: Later he also served as chief clerk of Jizhou.
idiomatic: Later he also served as chief clerk of Jizhou — so the record runs.

literal: When the Dacheng rebels rose, Bolin led the provincial army against them at Zhushao walled town and was killed by the rebels; he was posthumously made dragon-charging general and governor of Luozhou.
idiomatic: When the Dacheng rebels rose, Bolin led the provincial army against them at Zhushao and was killed; he was posthumously made dragon-charging general and governor of Luozhou.

literal: Boji was a legal affairs staff officer to Prince of Jingzhao Yu.
idiomatic: Boji was legal-affairs staff officer to the Prince of Jingzhao, Yu.

literal: When Yu rebelled, Boji would not follow and was killed; an edict posthumously made him governor of Donghai.
idiomatic: When Yu rebelled, Boji refused to follow and was killed; an edict posthumously made him governor of Donghai.

literal: Bofeng from youth was skilled in bow and horse; in maturity brave and strong in the arm.
idiomatic: Bofeng from youth was skilled with bow and horse; grown, he was bold and powerful.

literal: From court attendant and outer-office gentleman he was gradually promoted to general who pacifies the distance and forward general, and several times served as a commander.
idiomatic: From court attendant and outer-office gentleman he rose step by step to general who pacifies the distance and forward general and several times held field command.

literal: At the end of the Yong'an era, with the area commander Yuan Zigong he held Dan Valley and died in battle.
idiomatic: At the end of the Yong'an era he held Dan Valley with area commander Yuan Zigong and died in battle.

literal: The text is deficient.
idiomatic: The text is deficient — so the record runs.

literal: Zulong was a staff officer in the Ministry of Works.
idiomatic: Zulong was a staff officer in the ministry of works.

literal: By nature harsh and impetuous, after his father's death he contended with his elder brother Bolin over legitimacy of birth, each guarding himself with sword and blade as if against a foe.
idiomatic: Harsh and impetuous by nature, after his father's death he sued his elder brother Bolin over legitimacy of birth, each keeping sword and blade as against an enemy.

literal: Zuchi, childhood name Sheke, was rough in martial bearing and had physical strength.
idiomatic: Zuchi, childhood name Sheke, was rough and martial and strong in the arm.

literal: Inspector Yuan Luo installed him as acting commander-in-chief and led troops to attack sea bandits.
idiomatic: Inspector Yuan Luo installed him as acting commander-in-chief and led troops against sea bandits.

literal: At the beginning of the Putai era he rebelled together with Zhang Senghao and besieged Qingzhou.
idiomatic: At the opening of the Putai era he rebelled with Zhang Senghao and besieged Qingzhou.

literal: Erzhu Zhongyuan sent a general to suppress them; their heads were sent to the capital.
idiomatic: Erzhu Zhongyuan sent a general to crush them; their heads were sent to the capital.

literal: Zuqiu from youth loved learning; he drew the curtain and recited books, not striving with the age.
idiomatic: Zuqiu from youth loved learning; he studied behind closed curtains and did not vie with the world.

literal: Recommended as a cultivated talent, he did not accept.
idiomatic: Recommended as cultivated talent, he would not take office.

literal: Sengyuan's younger cousin He was governor of Pingchang.
idiomatic: Sengyuan's younger cousin He was governor of Pingchang — so the record runs.

literal: The household was immensely rich yet by nature stingy; he buried cash in hundreds of hu.
idiomatic: The house was immensely rich yet he was stingy by nature and buried cash in hundreds of hu.

literal: His mother Chunsi craved purslane; he begrudged the cash and would not buy it.
idiomatic: His mother Chunsi longed for purslane; he begrudged the money and would not buy it.

literal: His son Gui, styled Qize, stole a million in cash and fled, turning his back on He.
idiomatic: His son Gui, styled Qize, stole a million in cash and fled, abandoning He.

literal: Later he was a staff officer in the office of armor for the ceremonial peer with open office; convicted of corruption, he died at Jinyang.
idiomatic: Later he was armor-office staff officer to a ceremonial peer with open office; convicted of corruption, he died at Jinyang.

literal: Xuanbo's fellow commandery man Dong Mi.
idiomatic: Dong Mi came from Xuanbo's commandery.

literal: Mi's father Jing, together with Cui Kangshi of the same commandery, Huo Yuan of Guangyang, and others, all spread their great learning's fame through Liaohai.
idiomatic: Mi's father Jing, with Cui Kangshi of the same commandery, Huo Yuan of Guangyang, and others, all spread the fame of great learning through Liaohai.

literal: Mi loved learning and inherited his father's profession.
idiomatic: Mi loved learning and inherited his father's craft.

literal: When Zhongshan was pacified he entered court and was appointed Gentleman of the Protocol Section, drafting the rites for court audience, feasting, suburban sacrifice, and the altars of soil and grain.
idiomatic: When Zhongshan was pacified he entered court as gentleman of the protocol section and drafted the rites for court audience, banquets, suburban sacrifice, and the altars of soil and grain.

literal: Deng Yuan, styled Yanhai, was a man of Anding.
idiomatic: Deng Yuan, styled Yanhai, came from Anding.

literal: His grandfather Qiang was chariot general under Fu Jian.
idiomatic: His grandfather Qiang was chariot general under Fu Jian — so the record runs.

literal: His father Yi was governor of Hejian.
idiomatic: His father Yi was governor of Hejian — so the record runs.

literal: When Murong Chui besieged Ye, he made Yi rear general, inspector of Jizhou, and Marquis of Zhending.
idiomatic: When Murong Chui besieged Ye he made Yi rear general, inspector of Jizhou, and Marquis of Zhending.

literal: Yi wept and said to the envoy: "My late father was loyal to the house of Qin — how could Yi be first to rebel!
idiomatic: Yi wept and told the envoy: "My late father was loyal to Qin — how could Yi be the first to rebel?

literal: A loyal minister does not serve two lords — from antiquity the constant principle; I dare not hear the command.
idiomatic: A loyal minister does not serve two lords — that is the constant rule since antiquity; I dare not accept the order.

literal: " Chui sent an envoy to persuade him: "I and the chariot general became sworn brothers of different surnames; you too are like my own son or younger brother — how can you decline?
idiomatic: " Chui sent an envoy to persuade him: "Your grandfather the chariot general and I became sworn brothers of different surnames; you are like my own son or younger brother — how can you refuse?

literal: " Yi said: "Jizhou should be entrusted to kin and the worthy; Yi asks for another duty to offer his life.
idiomatic: " Yi said: "Jizhou should go to kin and the worthy; let Yi serve in another post and offer his life.

literal: " Chui thereupon employed him as General of Establishing Martiality, governor of Hejian, and Left Deputy Director of the Secretariat — in each post he won reputation.
idiomatic: " Chui then used him as general of establishing martiality, governor of Hejian, and left deputy director of the secretariat — in each post he won praise.

literal: He died as inner governor of Zhao commandery.
idiomatic: He died as inner governor of Zhao commandery — so the record runs.

literal: Yuan by nature was upright and plain; his words and conduct could be relied on; he ranged broadly through the classics; he excelled in the Changes and divination.
idiomatic: Yuan was upright and plain by nature, his words and conduct trustworthy; he ranged widely through the classics and excelled in the Changes and divination.

literal: When Taizu pacified the central plains he was promoted to Gentleman of the Composition Office.
idiomatic: When Taizu pacified the central plains he was raised to gentleman of the composition office.

literal: He went out as magistrate of Puqiu and cut down the crafty and violent; bandits were cleared away.
idiomatic: He went out as magistrate of Puqiu, cut down the crafty and violent, and cleared away bandits.

literal: He entered court as Gentleman of the Ministry of Personnel.
idiomatic: Recalled to court, he was made gentleman of the ministry of personnel.
